rule: a butting end held by another butt's through-fastener: one stud through the through bar, in one sleeve, into a bush in each of two coaxial opposite ends (§3.4, §4.5)
design: an RHS 200x100x4.75 of no system along +X; two 40x40 bars butting into it from +Y and from -Y on one centre line. c1 holds b2.a with a stud end (a stud, a bush, a sleeve cut to the bore, a Ø9 hole through the RHS); c2 holds b3.b with a bush end and is held_by c1. No error; each 40x40 550.00; one stud, two bushes, one sleeve 90.50 (the bore across the RHS's 100, less two 4.75 walls); one Ø9 hole through the RHS, from the face b2 meets; an M16 tap in each butting end. The stud crosses 100.00 between the two butting end faces. One butt with both ends and the stud end on each: two studs and two sleeves, and the hole through the RHS twice, a machining error. Two butts and no held_by: the fit error on c2. b3 moved 20 off b2's centre line: a connection error on c2. Held by a butt whose connector passes nothing through the RHS: a connection error on c2 (and c1's own fit error). The held end's connector passing its own stud: a connection error on c2
